beef-with-vegetables-excluding-carrots-b.title: Beef with vegetables (no carrots, broccoli, dark‑green leafy greens)

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef sautéed with a variety of vegetables, excluding carrots, broccoli and dark‑green leafy greens. Instead, sweet pepper, zucchini, tomatoes, onion and garlic are used. It is prepared without potatoes and served with mushroom sauce (1519).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is an excellent source of iron, zinc and vitamin B12.
Excluding carrots and broccoli reduces beta‑carotene content, giving the dish a more neutral flavor.
Mushroom sauce (1519) is often made from cream and button mushrooms, providing a creamy texture.
Such vegetable combinations are traditional in Mediterranean cuisine for a light yet satisfying meal.
The lack of potatoes makes the dish lower in carbohydrates, suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Beef supplies a complete set of essential amino acids needed for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B6 and B12 support nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Without potatoes or carrots, the dish helps keep blood sugar levels stable.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of mushroom sauce
items.content: Mushrooms contain selenium and polyphenols that combat free radicals.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Zinc from beef and vitamin C from tomatoes contribute to a stronger immune response.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Choose lean cuts of beef to keep saturated fat intake low.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: People with known mushroom allergies should avoid the mushroom sauce.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Prepared mushroom sauce can be salty; adjust added salt accordingly.

items.title: Risk of contamination if stored improperly
items.content: Beef should be kept at 4 °C or below and cooked thoroughly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the beef and vegetables hot, drizzled with mushroom sauce. The dish pairs well with whole‑grain sides, quinoa, or a fresh tomato salad. Garnish with herbs such as parsley or basil if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months. Reheat until the beef reaches an internal temperature of 75 °C.

content.title: About
content.content: Brussels sprouts are small, cabbage-like vegetables belonging to the cruciferous family. They originated in the Mediterranean region but are now cultivated in many temperate areas worldwide. Raw sprouts have a mildly bitter, nutty flavor and a crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vegetable is named after Brussels, where it was first cultivated in the 16th century.
It is one of the richest sources of vitamin K among vegetables.
Brussels sprouts contain glucoraphanin, a compound that may support the body’s detoxification processes.
Eating them raw preserves more vitamins than cooking.
In the 19th century Europeans often referred to them as “little cabbage.”

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is needed for DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: The sprouts contain glucoraphanin and other polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Cruciferous vegetables can cause increased gas production in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K intake may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to Brussels sprouts.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Raw sprouts can become contaminated with bacteria if not stored properly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw Brussels sprouts can be thinly sliced into salads, blended into smoothies, or used as a crunchy topping. They can also be lightly marinated in olive oil, lemon juice, and spices for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sprouts in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a ventilated container. Properly stored, they stay fresh for 1‑2 weeks. Discard any wilted or yellowing heads.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken back is the meat taken from the upper part of a bird's back. It is a lean cut with a tender texture and a mild flavor, suitable for frying, baking, and stewing.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken back contains less fat than the breast but more than the thigh.
It is commonly used in traditional Eastern European dishes such as stews and casseroles.
The bones left after trimming are rich in collagen and often used for broth making.
When cooked properly, the back stays juicy thanks to a modest amount of connective tissue.
In some countries the back is considered a delicacy and served as thinly sliced steaks.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken back provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with other poultry cuts, the back has a moderate fat content, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat contains vitamins B3, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken back supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Selenium and vitamin B6 in the meat help strengthen the body's immune defenses.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Insufficiently cooked meat may contain Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium in processed products
items.content: If the back is pre‑marinated, it can be high in salt, which is undesirable for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken back can be pan‑fried, baked, steamed, or braised in sauce. Before cooking, trim excess fat and skin, and cut the pieces into 1–2 cm thick strips for even cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh chicken back in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen back in the fridge before use.

content.title: About
content.content: The Italian sandwich (or sub) is a hearty sandwich made with a long soft roll filled with ham, salami, prosciutto, mozzarella, tomatoes, arugula, and aromatic herbs. Olive oil, balsamic vinegar and spices are often added. It is popular in fast‑food restaurants and cafés, served hot or cold.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Italian sandwich originated in the United States in the early 1920s, inspired by traditional Italian panini.
The classic bread is Italian ciabatta or a sub roll that soaks up sauces while staying slightly crunchy.
Original recipes often include pepperoni – thinly sliced spicy sausage.
The sandwich is commonly served with french fries or a fresh vegetable salad.
Some eateries add fragrant basil or oregano to boost flavor.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Meat fillings and cheese provide high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Sausages and bread contain niacin, thiamine and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil and mozzarella supply monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Tomatoes and arugula add vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.

items.title: Fiber from the bread
items.content: Whole‑grain ciabatta provides dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sausages and cheeses are often salty, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fat levels
items.content: Certain types of sausage and cheese may raise cholesterol.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Mozzarella can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A large sandwich can contain 500–800 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Nitrite content
items.content: Some cured meats contain nitrites, which can be harmful in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the sandwich hot, lightly toasted in an oven or grill so the cheese melts. Cut it in half and serve with marinara sauce or mustard. For a lighter version, use whole‑grain bread and lean ham slices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared sandwich can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. If the roll is sliced, wrap it tightly in plastic to prevent drying. Reheat in an oven or toaster before serving.

nutrition-bar-slim-fast-original-meal-ba.title: Nutrition bar (Slim Fast Original Meal Bar)

content.title: About
content.content: The Nutrition bar (Slim Fast Original Meal Bar) is a ready‑to‑eat protein bar designed as a full‑meal replacement. Each bar provides about 250 kcal, 9 g of protein, 5 g of fiber, and a balanced blend of vitamins and minerals, making it a convenient option for weight control and sustained energy throughout the day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bar is part of the Slim Fast line, a brand known since the 1970s for weight‑loss programs.
Each bar comes in an individual wrapper, perfect for on‑the‑go consumption.
It contains whole grains, soy protein, and whey protein, delivering a slow‑release energy profile.
No artificial colors or flavors are used—only natural flavor enhancers.
Slim Fast Original Meal Bar has been clinically tested as an effective component of diet plans.

items.title: Weight‑management support
items.content: A balanced mix of protein, carbs, and fats helps maintain satiety and reduces overeating.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from whole grains give an immediate energy boost, while protein sustains it.

items.title: Vitamin‑mineral complex
items.content: The bar is fortified with B‑vitamins, vitamin D, iron, and calcium, supporting overall metabolism.

items.title: Muscle‑mass preservation
items.content: 9 g of protein per bar assists in maintaining lean muscle during calorie restriction.

items.title: Convenience and portability
items.content: Individually wrapped, the bar is easy to include in travel, work, or outdoor activities.

items.title: Soy and dairy allergy
items.content: The bar contains soy and whey proteins, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content for low‑carb diets
items.content: Although formulated as a meal replacement, the bar does contain sugar, which may be unsuitable for strict low‑carb regimens.

items.title: Not a complete diet substitute
items.content: Relying solely on bars can lead to nutrient gaps; it’s best to combine them with whole foods.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Ingredients may include sucralose or acesulfame‑K, which some people prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is ready to eat straight from the wrapper. It works well as a breakfast, snack, or lunch replacement. For added variety, pair it with fresh fruit or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 7 days. For extended shelf life, refrigeration is optional but not required.
